prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid:
U+3D071. Left is a single vertical stem carrying THREE bars, with bottom bar LONGEST and middle shortest; no hanging flank legs. Central component: two rising prongs and outward arms crown a rounded arch. The arch LEFT course descends and curves inward but ends freely above baseline; its RIGHT course curves down-left into a long descending tail to baseline, leaving the arch OPEN at lower left. Inside it sits a separate small U/cup with TWO upper prongs and ONE horizontal crossbar creating ONE lower closed counter; the upper prong space stays OPEN. Use the coherent open-body THX/DYC construction, not a new closed enclosing oval. Right component: a top upright stem with a short RIGHT-projecting upper arm. This stem meets a lower horizontal which turns smoothly to the RIGHT, bends downward around a large bulge and returns diagonally down-left as a free terminal. INSIDE this bulge a separate short inward curved hook starts at upper left, turns right/down, crosses/joins the outer returning diagonal at a lower junction, and continues as a LONG DOWNWARD stem to the baseline. Keep the two major lower tails (central and right), the inner U counter, and the right crossing intact. Right short upper arm is shorter than its lower bent bar. All fine gaps visible, equal-width strokes only.

reading_criteria: Upper central fork must have two rising prongs and two lateral arms, not a three-upright trident.
Right outer returning diagonal must extend left beyond crossing with the inner hook/downstem as a free terminal.
Central small U has one closed lower counter and open upper prongs; outer arch remains open below.
